title: A relatively definable function on the realisations of a simple type is a power of the successor

standard_prerequisites.name: Aleph_0-saturation of the ambient model and compactness
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used inside the counted proof at lines 223, 231 and 236
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives surjectivity of the extension of f and lets the interval-wise behaviour found on a tail of C be transferred to the whole type p.

core_obligations: Show that f is surjective: the set p(x) together with the equation f-hat(x) = a is consistent for a in p(M), and saturation turns that into an actual preimage (proof line 223).

Show that f is injective: the preimage of f(a) inside the interval [c_0,a] is relatively definable and nonempty, so by clause (c) of the basic lemma it has a minimum a', and the corresponding minimality formula lies in p(x), which yields injectivity (proof line 224).

Show that f preserves the order: assuming not, the set of x with f-hat(a) <= f-hat(x) < x < a is nonempty for every a in p(M), and choosing a further element inside it exhibits a non-minimal point, contradicting clause (c) again (proof lines 226-229).

Identify the automorphism: compactness makes the extension increasing, an interval-isomorphism formula holds on a tail of C by a compactness argument and hence lies in p, and then f maps consecutive elements to consecutive elements on that tail, so f-hat agrees with a fixed power S^k of the successor on the tail and therefore on all of p (proof lines 231-243).
proof_roadmap: Prove that the definable function is an order automorphism of p(M), using the minimum clause for injectivity and for the order-preservation contradiction (proof lines 222-229).
Push the behaviour from a cofinite tail of C to the whole type by compactness and identify the shift power (proof lines 231-243).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that any relatively definable function f from the realisations of a simple type to itself is a power of the successor function with respect to the order that witnesses the type (statement lines 219-221). The proof first shows that f is an automorphism: surjectivity comes from saturation, injectivity from the minimum clause applied to a preimage inside a finite interval, and order preservation from a contradiction that again uses the minimum clause (proof lines 222-229). It then uses compactness to make the extension increasing, obtains an interval-isomorphism formula that holds on a cofinite tail of C and hence lies in the type, and concludes that f agrees with a fixed shift on that tail and therefore on the whole realisation set (proof lines 231-243). The step that carries the content is the last one, where the local interval behaviour is upgraded to a global description by compactness and the C-type property. H2.
